rule.message: Lead with what the reader gets. A headline that tells the searcher they are wrong argues with them instead of offering the benefit.
rule.fix: State the benefit the reader gets.

line: You don't need an agent sandbox
reason: The page answers people searching for an agent sandbox. Telling them they don't need one contradicts the search on purpose: it is the one claim they didn't expect, so they click to find out why, and the page then shows what they need instead. A benefit headline would read like every sandbox vendor's page in the same results.

The question is the reader's own worry, said the way they would think it, and the answer comes in the next three words. Rewritten as a statement it loses the moment of recognition that makes the line land.

line: "We ran it on Friday — by Monday the bill was gone," one engineer told us.
reason: It is a quote kept exactly as the person wrote it in their message. Changing their punctuation would put words in their mouth.
